grain_rule: One intuitive animal world (mammals); a niche is ONE body/trace/pattern system. This registry sits AHEAD of the broad niches.json registry in the campaign queue.
pattern: (a) raw capture taken the same way across many individuals/species; (b) used for individual ID or age/sex/species reading, labels in old catalogues/forensic atlases/photo-ID archives/museum cast collections, often on a second ruler (DNA, tags, dissection); (c) instantly headline-shaped.
koala_verification: Henneberg, Lambert & Leigh (1997), 'Fingerprint homoplasy: koalas and humans', Univ. of Adelaide: ~20 koalas, ink prints + SEM; ridges nearly identical to human in microscopic morphology, pattern organisation and individual uniqueness; authors called a crime-scene mix-up 'extremely unlikely'; no documented crime-scene confusion exists.

niches.name: Primate fingerprints & dermatoglyphic archives
niches.family: A. Skin prints — fingers, palms, pads & noses
niches.score_justification: The original fingerprint science was built on animal prints too — Cummins-era dermatoglyphic collections cover dozens of primate species, ridge counts never re-joined across collections.
keywords: ape monkey fingerprint ridge count data

fidelity_card.RAW: Ink and rolled fingerprints, palm prints and dermatoglyphic tracings in anthropology and forensic collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One finger/palm — thousands of prints across dozens of primate species in the classic collections, one ink-print protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species/individual called from ridge pattern vs DNA taxonomy of the same zoo/museum animals (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Zoo studbooks and museum specimens tied to print cards

niches.headline_shape: Police once fingerprinted the chimps at a zoo to rule them out of a crime — the apes' prints were that close to ours.
niches.why_niche: Dermatoglyphics was a mid-century industry whose collections sit in anthropology departments and forensic museums; genetics replaced it before its cross-species ridge data was ever pooled.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign7: Campaign 7: Galton surface is digitised and openly served by Wellcome (SILVER, mostly human); the primate subset (Weldon chimp bundle, Penrose) is closed-stores, catalogue-only. No stranded file pile exists to recover.

niches.name: Cattle muzzle (nose) print registration archives
niches.family: A. Skin prints — fingers, palms, pads & noses
niches.score_justification: The biggest fingerprint-style archive in the animal world: Japan's Wagyu Registry has ink muzzle prints for 3M+ beef cattle since 1948 — and it is a paper/card system.

fidelity_card.RAW: Ink muzzle prints lifted on paper/cards at registration (before 4 months, again after 14 months in the Japanese system), plus modern muzzle photographs
fidelity_card.UNIT: One muzzle — millions registered in Japan since 1948, thousands in Petersen-era and university series elsewhere, one ink-lift protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Muzzle print ID vs ear-tag / RFID / DNA pedigree records for the same animals (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The Wagyu Registry Association's own registration certificates (nose print + pedigree on one card)

niches.headline_shape: Japan has fingerprinted its finest cattle by nose since 1948 — over three million cows, each with a print card like a criminal record.
niches.why_niche: The registration archives are institutional paper; the computer-vision literature trains on a few hundred fresh photos and has never touched the historical card millions.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign7: Campaign 7: KILL-for-recovery — zero digital surface anywhere probed; the 3M+ print archive is paper/certificate by design. Score cut reflects hunter-recoverable gold only; the custody finding stands (see calibration).

niches.name: Paw-track morphometrics & FIT footprint archives
niches.score_justification: WildTrack's FIT extracts 120+ measures per print and reports >90% species/sex/age accuracy across 13+ species — yet each species training set lives with its project, captive-known prints are the rarest data in tracking.

fidelity_card.RAW: Footprint photographs taken to one ruler-and-slip protocol (WildTrack FIT and its predecessors), plus hand-measured track tables
fidelity_card.UNIT: One print/trail — training sets of known captive individuals per species, field trails by the thousand, 13+ species with FIT algorithms
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Individual/sex/age called from print vs the known captive animal or collared wild animal that made it (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Captive-animal known-identity trail sets (the FIT training gold standard)

niches.headline_shape: A photograph of a footprint can name the tiger, its sex and its age — trackers always knew; the measurement files proving it sit project by project.
niches.why_niche: FIT standardised the capture but not the custody: species datasets sit with NGOs, zoos and consultancies, and the pre-FIT hand-measured track tables were never digitised at all.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign7: Campaign 7: KILL — FIT training libraries (tapir 426 imgs/36 indiv.; otter CNN 2,500 imgs) are project-held; software is a JMP add-in by request; no per-species file piles on any surface probed.

niches.name: Whale fluke trailing-edge photo-ID catalogues
niches.score_justification: 39 North-Pacific catalogues were unified by Happywhale (27,956 individuals) — proof of value AND the narrowing: the un-joined remainder is film-era, Southern Ocean and non-humpback catalogues.

fidelity_card.RAW: Fluke photographs (film-era prints/slides and digital) in regional whale research catalogues
fidelity_card.UNIT: One fluke — tens of thousands of individuals globally; 39 catalogues in the North Pacific alone, one underside-photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Fluke match vs genetic sample taken at the same encounter (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The Happywhale/NPPID unified North Pacific set as the benchmark of what joining yields

niches.headline_shape: Every humpback's tail is a fingerprint in black and white — the world spent 50 years photographing them and is only now joining the albums.
niches.why_niche: Happywhale joined the North Pacific digital era; the pre-digital slide cabinets, the Southern Ocean and Atlantic regional catalogues, and sperm-whale fluke sets remain separate piles.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign7: Campaign 7: best host (Juneau) is a published edition stack (SILVER); niche-wide the pattern was professionalised into Happywhale/Flukebook platforms. Strandedness over-predicted.

niches.name: Dolphin dorsal-fin notch catalogues
niches.score_justification: Sarasota alone holds 5,000+ fin images since 1970 and GoMDIS joins 35 Gulf catalogues (23,444 animals) — outside the Gulf, hundreds of FinBase-era catalogues never joined anything.

fidelity_card.RAW: Dorsal-fin photographs and FinBase/Access-era catalogue databases on lab and institute sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One fin — hundreds of regional catalogues, hundreds to thousands of individuals each, one trailing-edge protocol since Würsig 1977
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Fin ID vs freeze-brand/tag/genetic identity of the same dolphin (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Sarasota's known-history individuals (births/deaths observed since 1970)

niches.headline_shape: A dolphin's fin collects nicks like a passport collects stamps — labs have filed the passports bay by bay for fifty years.
niches.why_niche: FinBase standardised hundreds of local catalogues on desktop databases that were never networked; GoMDIS proved joining works for one gulf and stopped there.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign7: Campaign 7: best public set (Beaufort) is a formal-archive DOI subset (INVENTORY); master catalogues are lab-held or researcher-only (GoMDIS). FinBase-era piles did not surface on the web.

niches.name: Elephant ear edge, tear & vein ID archives
niches.score_justification: Amboseli has ID'd 1,600+ elephants since 1972 by ear tears/holes/veins on physical ID cards; every long-term site (Gorongosa, Mara, Samburu…) keeps its own card tradition.

fidelity_card.RAW: Photographic ear ID cards (physical card files, later digital) recording ear edge tears, holes and vein patterns, per long-term study site
fidelity_card.UNIT: One ear — 1,600+ known individuals at Amboseli, hundreds to thousands per other site, one card-and-photo protocol per site tradition
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Ear ID vs DNA from dung/biopsy and vs tusk/body marks recorded on the same card (second rulers)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Amboseli's known-birth individuals (exact ages since 1972)

niches.headline_shape: An elephant's ear is a torn, veined map no other elephant shares — researchers have carried its ID cards in Land Cruiser gloveboxes for fifty years.
niches.why_niche: The ID-card tradition is per-site and partly still physical; Gorongosa's Who's Who went digital behind a password, Amboseli's cards span paper and digital, and no cross-site ear archive exists.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign7: Campaign 7: KILL/INVENTORY — ID cards stay in project custody (Who's Who password-protected by design); elephant.se is a published database mirror, not the card archive; ATE unreachable from this client.

niches.name: Whisker-spot (vibrissae) pattern catalogues — lions & pinnipeds
niches.family: F. Faces, ears, eyes, scars, tails & whiskers
niches.score_justification: Pennycuick & Rudnai's 1970 lion method is pure pattern: dot maps of whisker follicles, still used in Kruger/India (WII's Lion software) and re-invented for sea lions — three literatures, one geometry, zero joining.

fidelity_card.RAW: Whisker-spot dot maps and muzzle photographs in lion and pinniped ID catalogues
fidelity_card.UNIT: One muzzle — hundreds of lions per park catalogue (method since 1970), pinniped sets of 50–1,000, dot-map protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Whisker ID vs scar/ear-mark ID and genetic ID in the same individuals (second rulers)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Australian sea lion known-individual sets used to validate the method (99% pattern uniqueness at n=50)

niches.headline_shape: A lion's whisker dots are a star chart printed on its muzzle — rangers have read the same chart since 1970 and kept it park by park.
niches.why_niche: The lion, sea-lion and seal whisker literatures cite different ancestors and hold separate catalogues; the shared point-pattern geometry has never been run across them.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign7: Campaign 7: KILL for catalogues — Desert Lion's file surface is field-photo galleries + published reports (INVENTORY); no whisker-pattern file pile on any host probed; sea-lion validation set is literature-only.

niches.name: Mammal guard-hair scale casts & hair atlases (wildlife forensics)
niches.score_justification: The Texas atlas alone covers 150+ species with SEM scale images; ZSI Kolkata, FBI/USFWS-style labs and Brunner & Coman built parallel atlases on three continents that cite different standards.
keywords: guard hair scale cast identification atlas
mammal hair atlas SEM scale pattern

fidelity_card.RAW: Cuticular scale casts (gelatin/cellulose impressions), SEM surface images and photomicrographs in forensic hair atlases
fidelity_card.UNIT: One hair — 150+ species in the Texas atlas, 100+ in the Indian and Australian atlases, one cast-and-mount protocol per atlas tradition
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species called from scale cast vs DNA barcoding of the same hair/specimen (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Museum-vouchered hairs (atlas specimens tied to skins/skulls)

niches.headline_shape: A single guard hair carries a scale pattern like a fingerprint — forensic atlases were built continent by continent and never checked against each other.
niches.why_niche: Hair ID is a forensic service literature: regional atlases (Texas 2009, ZSI series, Brunner & Coman 1974) each keyed their own fauna with their own scale vocabulary.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign8: Campaign 8: material and loose-file hosting real (CMU personal pages, 57 species), but every surface is a deliberate publication — atlas PDFs, teaching pages, journal trees. Strandedness over-predicted; SILVER ceiling at the surfaces checked. 9 -> 8.

niches.name: Koala fingerprint collections
niches.family: A. Skin prints — fingers, palms, pads & noses
niches.score_justification: Headline is perfect and verified (Henneberg 1997), but the known print population is small — one species, tens of documented individuals — so archive depth caps the score.

fidelity_card.RAW: Ink prints and SEM fingertip images from wildlife-park and university anatomy collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One fingertip — one species, tens of individuals in the published study, unknown numbers in zoo/wildlife-park files, one ink-print protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Koala ridge pattern vs human prints in the same forensic reference files (the second ruler is our own fingerprint system)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The 1997 Adelaide reference prints (Henneberg, Lambert & Leigh)

niches.headline_shape: A koala's fingerprint is nearly indistinguishable from a human's under a microscope — verified in 1997, and no, it has never actually turned up at a crime scene.
niches.why_niche: One famous study, then near-silence: wildlife parks handle koalas daily and no print collection was ever built on the 1997 foundation.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign8: Campaign 8: decisively falsified as a file hunt — no collection host exists anywhere probed; the surface is two small papers (n~20 + n=3). Any larger set is in Henneberg's Adelaide custody, offline. Paper-only. 8 -> 5.

niches.name: Dog nose-print archives
niches.family: A. Skin prints — fingers, palms, pads & noses
niches.score_justification: Petersen took 350+ animal nose prints in 1922; kennel clubs and insurers ran nose-print registries for decades — paper archives, modern apps are rebuilding from zero.

fidelity_card.RAW: Ink nose prints on index cards and nose photographs in kennel-club, insurer and lab collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One nose — registries ran to thousands of dogs; the 2021 viability study re-proved uniqueness on 70 dogs / 19 breeds, one ink-or-camera protocol per era
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Nose pattern ID vs microchip/tag records for the same dogs (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Longitudinal re-prints of the same dog months apart (pattern invariance series)

niches.headline_shape: Your dog's nose print is its fingerprint — kennel clubs were filing them on index cards a century ago.
niches.why_niche: Historic nose-print registries were paper and breed-club local; the smartphone-era startups each built tiny private datasets and none inherited the card archives.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign8: Campaign 8: historic archive is CKC paper/microfiche custody (1938-1992); modern sets are by-request (Korean study) or vanished platform data (Ant Group). No loose archive exists. 8 -> 6.

niches.name: Plaster track-cast museum collections
niches.score_justification: Museums hold drawers of plaster paw casts — snow leopard, wolf, lynx — made when casts were the data; catalogued as objects, never measured as a set.

fidelity_card.RAW: Plaster and latex track casts with specimen labels in natural-history museum collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One cast — hundreds per large collection, dozens of species, one cast-making tradition across a century
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species/sex on the cast label vs the cast re-measured today against FIT-style morphometrics (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Casts tied to collected specimens or known zoo animals

niches.headline_shape: Before cameras, scientists carried plaster to the snow and poured the footprint itself — museums still hold the drawers of poured paws.
niches.why_niche: Cast collections were catalogued by accession, not by measurement; nobody has run a single morphometric pass across a museum's cast drawers.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign8: Campaign 8: physical museum custody + formal specimen databases (Smithsonian DwC-A) + one approval-gated 3D platform (Idaho VM). No loose cast file pile anywhere probed; Murie collection has no online surface. 8 -> 6.

niches.name: Elephant footprint age-estimation archives
niches.score_justification: Forefoot circumference converts to shoulder height and age; the calibration sets (known-age Amboseli elephants walking in sand) are small, old and priceless.

fidelity_card.RAW: Footprint photographs and forefoot-circumference measurement sheets from known-age elephant studies and ranger monitoring
fidelity_card.UNIT: One footprint — calibration series from known-age individuals (Amboseli), monitoring trails by the thousand across Africa/Asia
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Age read from the footprint vs the elephant's known birth year in the long-term ID catalogues (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Amboseli known-age individuals measured directly

niches.headline_shape: You can read an elephant's age off the print its front foot leaves in the dust — if you have the calibration walks, and almost nobody kept them.
niches.why_niche: The method is used by rangers everywhere; the underlying known-age measurement series live in a few theses and project files from the 1980s–2000s.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign8: Campaign 8: the calibration-grade data is either already formally published (Parker/UF IR, 3,199 cases as CSV) or custody-only (ATE Access databases). Method's data layer is integrated/custodial, not stranded. 8 -> 7.

niches.name: Right-whale head callosity catalogues
niches.score_justification: The callosity pattern is read from aerial photos since the 1970s; the North Atlantic consortium catalogue is curated but the southern-hemisphere catalogues (Argentina, South Africa, Australia) grew separately.

fidelity_card.RAW: Aerial and boat photographs of head callosity patterns in consortium and regional catalogues
fidelity_card.UNIT: One head — ~400 living North Atlantic individuals, thousands in southern catalogues, aerial-photo protocol since Payne's 1970s work
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Callosity ID vs genetic profiles from biopsy of the same whales (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium catalogue as the curated anchor

niches.headline_shape: The rough white patches on a right whale's head are as fixed as a face — whale watchers have read them from planes since the seventies.
niches.why_niche: Three ocean basins built three callosity catalogues in three institutions; cross-basin matching (whales do cross) rests on personal correspondence, not a joined archive.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign8: Campaign 8: one small SILVER (EBRWS live catalogue-brochure stack); the big systems are consortium/platform custody (NARWC researcher-only by written protocol, ARWPIC, Flukebook). The Juneau pattern repeated one niche over. 8 -> 7.

niches.name: Manatee scar & tail photo-ID system archives
niches.score_justification: Florida's MIPS system has matched manatees by scars/tail notches since the 1970s — a state-run pattern archive with sketch-era roots, mirrored by separate Caribbean/Brazil sets.

fidelity_card.RAW: Underwater photographs and hand-drawn scar sketches in the Manatee Photo-ID System and sister programmes
fidelity_card.UNIT: One manatee — thousands of individuals in Florida alone since the 1970s, sketch-then-photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Scar-pattern ID vs PIT-tag/genetic identity recorded at rescue/health assessments (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Rescued manatees whose identity is known absolutely at release

niches.headline_shape: A manatee is known by its propeller scars — the state of Florida keeps a mugshot file, part sketchbook, part database.
niches.why_niche: MIPS is an agency system with restricted doors; the sketch-era archive and the non-Florida programmes were never part of any public pattern set.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign8: Campaign 8: GOLD — Hartley's frozen April-2013 Practical Scar Sheet set (~200 Blue Spring individuals) stranded on the SMC archive subdomain, absent from MIPS, sample-verified and visually inspected. Score raised on confirmation (frog-call precedent). 8 -> 9.

niches.name: Rhino ear-notch & horn-profile ID records
niches.score_justification: Distinct from the landed rhino forearm work: this is the applied ID system — ear notches cut by managers plus horn silhouette profiles, kept per-reserve in sighting books. (Forearm centroid work excluded.)
keywords: rhino sighting book ear notch archive

fidelity_card.RAW: Ear-notch diagrams, horn-profile photographs and sighting-book pages from reserves and rhino monitoring programmes
fidelity_card.UNIT: One rhino — hundreds per reserve, thousands across programmes, notch-code + profile-photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Notch/horn ID vs DNA from ear-tissue taken at the notching itself, and horn DNA (RhODIS) (second rulers)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: RhODIS forensic horn-DNA database as the cross-check anchor

niches.headline_shape: Rhino managers cut a code into the ear and read the horn's silhouette like a skyline — each reserve keeps its own skyline book.
niches.why_niche: Ear-notching is universal practice and per-reserve paperwork; horn profiles accumulate in monitoring photos that no cross-reserve system ingests.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign11: Campaign 11: KILL for recovery — notch/horn records are per-reserve anti-poaching custody; the anchor (RhODIS, 180,000+ samples by 2024) is a law-enforcement forensic system. No file surface anywhere probed. 8 -> 6.

niches.name: Pinniped pelage-pattern photo-ID (ringed & monk seals)
niches.score_justification: Saimaa's SealID set (57 seals, 2,080 images) proved a pelage dataset can be published — and exposed how many seal colonies still match patterns by eye from slide boxes.

fidelity_card.RAW: Seal flank photographs (slides, then digital) in colony photo-ID catalogues
fidelity_card.UNIT: One flank pattern — hundreds of individuals per colony catalogue (Saimaa ~400 animals; Cap Blanc monk seals since 1993), haul-out photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Pelage ID vs flipper-tag / telemetry identity of the same seal (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: SealID's expert-matched public benchmark set (57 individuals, 2,080 images)

niches.headline_shape: A ringed seal wears a fingerprint made of rings over its whole body — no two seals have ever worn the same one.
niches.why_niche: Each seal colony's catalogue belongs to its research group; slide-era catalogues (monk seals 1990s) predate the ML datasets and were never digitised into them.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign11: Campaign 11: SILVER ceiling — flagship (SealID, 57 seals/2,080 images) is a deliberate DOI release in Fairdata; colony catalogues are programme/agency custody (Cap Blanc slides; NOAA InPort 'No Distributions available'). 8 -> 7.

niches.name: Tiger stripe-pattern camera-trap catalogues
niches.family: D. Coat patterns — stripes, rosettes, spots & scales
niches.score_justification: Every tiger's stripes are mapped by camera traps nationally, but the catalogues are security-sealed per country/programme; the pattern data behind published counts is the stranded layer.
keywords: camera trap tiger individual identification data

fidelity_card.RAW: Camera-trap flank photographs and stripe-matching files in national and NGO tiger programmes
fidelity_card.UNIT: One flank — thousands of individuals across range countries, standard paired-camera protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Stripe ID vs genetic ID from scat collected in the same grids (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: India's national tiger estimation archive as the (restricted) anchor set

niches.headline_shape: No two tigers share a stripe map — countries count their tigers from stripe photographs and then lock the photographs away.
niches.why_niche: Counts are published, pattern files are not; each programme's catalogue is a silo justified by poaching risk, so cross-border tigers are matched by personal contact.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign11: Campaign 11: KILL for recovery — the real catalogue is India's national NTCA/WII archive, restricted by design (poaching); only public stripe files are the ExtractCompare demo handful (INVENTORY). 8 -> 6.

niches.name: Leopard & jaguar rosette catalogues
niches.family: D. Coat patterns — stripes, rosettes, spots & scales
niches.score_justification: Rosettes ID individuals across hundreds of separate camera-trap studies; Wildbook ingests some, the long tail of thesis-era catalogues is the niche.
keywords: leopard rosette pattern camera trap data

fidelity_card.RAW: Camera-trap rosette photographs and matching spreadsheets from individual study sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One rosette flank — dozens to hundreds of individuals per study, hundreds of studies, paired-camera protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Rosette ID vs GPS-collar/genetic identity in the same study animals (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Long-term sites (e.g. Cockscomb jaguars, since the 1980s) with known individuals

niches.headline_shape: A jaguar's rosettes are a star-map only it wears — every valley's researchers keep their own atlas of the same sky.
niches.why_niche: Camera-trap science is study-shaped: each project publishes a density estimate and keeps its rosette catalogue in a drawer or a dead laptop.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign11: Campaign 11: field catalogues are project custody / Wildbook-ingested fraction; public surface is ExtractCompare demos (INVENTORY). Long-tail thesis catalogues unprobed individually, so the cut is one step, not two. 8 -> 7.

niches.name: Zebra stripe-pattern ID archives
niches.family: D. Coat patterns — stripes, rosettes, spots & scales
niches.score_justification: Stripe ID began with hand-drawn zebra codes in the 1960s (Petersen 1972); Grevy's/plains catalogues per ecosystem, plus the famous mare-foal recognition experiments' photo files.

fidelity_card.RAW: Stripe photographs and hand-coded stripe diagrams from ecosystem monitoring programmes
fidelity_card.UNIT: One flank/shoulder pattern — thousands of individuals in the large ecosystem catalogues, photo protocol since the film era
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Stripe ID vs ear-notch/collar/genetic identity in the same herds (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Long-term known-individual herds (e.g. Grevy's in Kenya) as anchor

niches.headline_shape: A zebra's stripes are a barcode its own foal learns by heart — scientists have been photocopying the barcodes since the sixties.
niches.why_niche: Zebra ID moved from drawn codes to StripeSpotter-era software per project; the drawn-code archives and most ecosystem catalogues were never merged.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign11: Campaign 11: SILVER ceiling — public layer is deliberate releases (GZGC via LILA; StripeSpotter 2011); drawn-code era is paper, ecosystem catalogues did not surface. 8 -> 7.

niches.name: Giraffe coat-pattern ID archives
niches.family: D. Coat patterns — stripes, rosettes, spots & scales
niches.score_justification: Giraffe spots are lifelong and individual; tower-by-tower catalogues across Africa, Wildbook for Giraffe ingests a fraction — the rest are ranger/guide photo files.

fidelity_card.RAW: Flank/torso coat-pattern photographs in reserve and research catalogues
fidelity_card.UNIT: One torso pattern — hundreds to thousands per population catalogue, right-flank photo convention
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Coat ID vs GPS-collar and genetic identity in monitored populations (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Long-term Serengeti/Murchison known-individual sets

niches.headline_shape: A giraffe wears its name in patches big enough to read from a safari vehicle — every reserve reads a different page.
niches.why_niche: Tourism and research both photograph giraffes constantly; the ID catalogues sit with individual reserves and guides' hard drives, Wildbook coverage notwithstanding.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign11: Campaign 11: SILVER ceiling via GZGC giraffe subset; living system is the GiraffeSpotter Wildbook platform (custody by design); reserve catalogues did not surface. 8 -> 7.

niches.name: Tooth-wear age charts & jaw collections (deer and game)
niches.score_justification: Every game agency aged deer by tooth wear from chart sets built on a handful of known-age jaws; the jaw collections behind rival charts were never compared head-to-head.
keywords: tooth wear age chart deer known age
tooth eruption wear ageing jaw collection
red deer jaw age data archive
game animal tooth wear reference photographs

fidelity_card.RAW: Jaw photographs/specimens and wear-score sheets in agency and university game collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One jaw — known-age reference sets of hundreds per species; agency-scored jaws by the hundred thousand, standard wear-chart protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Wear age vs cementum-annuli age from the same jaw (second ruler — the classic two-rulers pair)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Known-age penned deer/elk herds whose jaws built the original charts

niches.headline_shape: A deer's teeth are a clock every hunter is taught to read — the clock was set from a few hundred jaws and never re-checked against the true ages.
niches.why_niche: Wear charts are regional (each agency its own poster) and their reference jaw collections sit in freezers and museum drawers, un-cross-validated.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign11: Campaign 11: SILVER chart stack (TPWD, Boone & Crockett, TPWD guide afterlife), but the headline two-rulers comparison was already run and published (Foley et al. 2021, known-age n=134 + harvested n=5,117). 8 -> 7.

niches.name: Cementum-annuli tooth-age laboratory archives
niches.score_justification: One lab (Matson's) has sectioned teeth since 1969 for agencies continent-wide — annuli counts vs the wear ages and harvest records on the same animals are a ready two-rulers panel.

fidelity_card.RAW: Tooth cross-section images and annuli count records in ageing-lab and agency files
fidelity_card.UNIT: One tooth — hundreds of thousands of teeth sectioned across species since 1969, one histology protocol per lab
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Cementum age vs tooth-wear age and vs known age for marked animals (two second rulers)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Known-age marked bears/deer submitted blind to the labs

niches.headline_shape: Slice a tooth and count the winters in its root — the labs that do it hold a half-century of slices nobody lined up against the ages everyone guessed in the field.
niches.why_niche: Ageing is a service industry: labs return a number, agencies file it, and the section images plus the field guesses were never joined into one audit set.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign11: Campaign 11: KILL for recovery — service-industry custody (Matson's, since 1969): ages are client deliverables, sections/field guesses never joined publicly; the one loose full report (MN DNR 2006) is 404 with no Wayback copy found. 8 -> 6.

niches.name: Primate & chimpanzee face-pattern ID archives
niches.family: F. Faces, ears, eyes, scars, tails & whiskers
niches.score_justification: Chimp faces were ID'd by human eye at Gombe/Taï for 60 years; ChimpFace-era ML now trains on scraped sets while the sites' own portrait archives stay home.

fidelity_card.RAW: Portrait ID photographs and face-description cards from long-term primate field sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One face — hundreds of known individuals per site (Gombe since 1960), thousands across sites, portrait protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Face ID vs genetic ID from faecal DNA of the same chimps (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Known-pedigree individuals at the long-term sites

niches.headline_shape: Researchers at Gombe know two hundred chimpanzee faces the way you know your family's — the portrait files that taught them are still at the field stations.
niches.why_niche: Face archives are field-site patrimony; the ML community built its own small scraped datasets rather than joining the sites' sixty years of portraits.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign11: Campaign 11: INVENTORY — ML world scraped its own published set (ChimpFace 5,559/90) while site portrait archives (Gombe/JGI) stay field-site patrimony. 8 -> 7.

niches.name: Primate & clinical palm/sole dermatoglyphics (atd angle archives)
niches.family: A. Skin prints — fingers, palms, pads & noses
niches.score_justification: Palmar atd angles and sole patterns fill medical-genetics archives (Down syndrome diagnostics era) plus primate atlases; two literatures never met.

fidelity_card.RAW: Palm and sole prints with measured atd angles and pattern maps, in clinical genetics files and primate atlases
fidelity_card.UNIT: One palm/sole — thousands of clinical prints, hundreds of primate specimens, one measurement convention
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Pattern diagnosis from prints vs chromosome/DNA diagnosis of the same patients and species (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Karyotyped clinical series and museum primate material

niches.headline_shape: Doctors once read a baby's palm the way they now read its chromosomes — the angle in the palm was a genetic test.
niches.why_niche: Clinical dermatoglyphics died the day karyotyping arrived; its print archives sit in medical-school files, unlinked to the primate dermatoglyphic collections that used the same measures.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: KILL paper-only in C12: no print-archive surface; the atd-vs-karyotype comparison was already published by the literature itself (1970, replicated 2023). Premise (an unlinked archive) false on the web. 7 -> 5.

niches.name: Paw-pad surface & ridge pattern atlases (bears, raccoons, carnivores)
niches.family: A. Skin prints — fingers, palms, pads & noses
niches.score_justification: Pad photos/casts are how trackers separate look-alike species; pad atlases are regional, hand-drawn era, never pooled.

fidelity_card.RAW: Paw-pad photographs, casts and drawn pad maps in tracking atlases and museum collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One pad — dozens of carnivore/omnivore species per atlas, hundreds of specimens, standard pad-on-glass or cast protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species called from pad pattern vs the track/trail it came from and DNA from scat at the same site (second rulers)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Zoo and museum specimens photographed pad-up

niches.headline_shape: A raccoon's hand looks eerily like a tiny human hand — and its palm print is in the tracking atlases to prove it.
niches.why_niche: Tracking literature is a cottage world of regional guides; the pad reference photos behind them live in authors' and museums' files, not in any shared atlas.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: INVENTORY in C12: canonical guides openly digitised (Murie full text, Amherst sheet); no pad-pattern archive surface; cast collections already killed in C8. 7 -> 6.

niches.name: Bear paw mensuration & harvest track records
niches.score_justification: Agencies measured hind-foot length on harvested bears for a century to sex/age them; the ledgers predate DNA sexing and were never audited against it.
keywords: bear hind foot length sex identification

fidelity_card.RAW: Paw measurement cards/ledgers from harvest check stations, plus track-measurement tables in agency reports
fidelity_card.UNIT: One paw — thousands of harvested bears per jurisdiction across decades, one measuring-board protocol per agency
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Sex/age from paw size vs DNA/tooth-cementum determination on the same bear (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Check-station bears with both paw cards and cementum ages

niches.headline_shape: A dead bear's back foot was measured to guess its sex — the guess was written down for fifty years before anyone checked it against DNA.
niches.why_niche: Harvest records are jurisdiction paperwork; the paw-size rules in the hunting guides descend from ledgers nobody re-audited.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: INVENTORY/KILL in C12: the one long-run paw-width series (Hokkaido 1976-2015) is a formal data paper; harvest paw-card ledgers surfaced nowhere. 7 -> 6.

niches.name: Wolf & canid track-size survey archives
niches.score_justification: Wolf-vs-dog-vs-coyote by track size is a live forensic question in rewilding Europe/North America; survey track tables sit in agency PDFs.

fidelity_card.RAW: Track measurement tables (length/width/gait) from wolf and carnivore snow surveys, agency reports and tracker archives
fidelity_card.UNIT: One track set — thousands per national survey across decades, ruler-in-photo or calliper protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species called from the track vs DNA from scat/hair collected on the same survey line (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Tracks of known captive wolves, dogs and coyotes measured the same way

niches.headline_shape: A wolf and a big dog leave nearly the same footprint — the argument about which one crossed the farm is settled from tables nobody has pooled.
niches.why_niche: Each country's monitoring programme publishes summary presence maps; the measurement-level track tables stay in project reports and trackers' notebooks.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: INVENTORY/KILL in C12: measurement-level track data exists only as a formal NASA archive deposit (ORNL DAAC 2188, shared with snow-track); agency surveys publish summary reports only. 7 -> 6.

niches.name: Snow-track gait & stride archives (lynx, wolverine, mustelids)
niches.score_justification: Nordic snow-tracking transects recorded stride/gait patterns for decades — a designed comparable set, province by province.

fidelity_card.RAW: Snow-transect record cards and gait diagrams from Nordic and boreal wildlife triangle / survey schemes
fidelity_card.UNIT: One track crossing — tens of thousands of transect crossings per country across decades, standard route protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species from gait pattern vs camera/DNA confirmation in the same survey areas (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Finland's wildlife-triangle long-run series as the published benchmark

niches.headline_shape: In deep snow an animal writes its name in stride — surveyors read the same script every winter for forty years and filed it by province.
niches.why_niche: Snow tracking is a Nordic institutional tradition with paper-era roots; digitisation happened province by province and the gait-level records were left behind the presence counts.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: INVENTORY/KILL in C12: NASA deposit is formal; Finland's wildlife triangles are an institute programme publishing crossing counts, gait-level records never a file surface. 7 -> 6.

niches.name: Elephant tusk shape & configuration records
niches.score_justification: Tusk shape is the second ID feature on every elephant card and the trait poaching selects on (Gorongosa tusklessness) — but it changes with breakage, capping the score.

fidelity_card.RAW: Tusk shape/configuration fields and photographs inside elephant ID databases and ivory-seizure records
fidelity_card.UNIT: One tusk pair — thousands of registered individuals across site databases, card-description protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Tusk ID vs ear ID on the same individual (second ruler — two pattern systems, one animal)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Seized-ivory DNA assignments back to populations (the forensic anchor)

niches.headline_shape: An elephant's tusks are as personal as handwriting — and in one park, war selected the elephants whose tusks never grew.
niches.why_niche: Tusk data rides inside ear-ID databases and seizure labs, never extracted as its own cross-site pattern record.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: KILL custody in C12: tusk configuration is a field inside the password/admin Who's Who database, not a file archive. 7 -> 6.

niches.name: Cheetah spot & tear-mark ID files
niches.family: D. Coat patterns — stripes, rosettes, spots & scales
niches.score_justification: Cheetah ID leans on spot patterns plus tail rings and tear marks; Serengeti's decades of ID photos are one project, farm-level Namibian files are another world.
keywords: cheetah tear marks tail rings ID

fidelity_card.RAW: Spot-pattern ID photographs and drawn ID sheets from long-term cheetah projects and farmer/researcher files
fidelity_card.UNIT: One flank/face — hundreds of known individuals in the Serengeti project alone since the 1970s, photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Spot ID vs radio-collar/genetic identity in the same animals (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Serengeti Cheetah Project's known-pedigree individuals

niches.headline_shape: A cheetah can be told from its spots and the black tear-lines on its face — the projects that learned the faces never shared the album.
niches.why_niche: Fewer, larger projects than leopards, but the same shape: ID albums are project property, and the pre-digital Serengeti sheets are one fire away from loss.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: INVENTORY/KILL in C12: papers/reports public (Kelly 2001 on personal site, Mara-Meru 2022); the 10k/90k photo albums are project custody. 7 -> 6.

niches.name: Snow leopard rosette & tail catalogues
niches.family: D. Coat patterns — stripes, rosettes, spots & scales
niches.score_justification: The hardest coat catalogue: 12 range countries, tiny densities, every programme's rosette files precious and separate; scores capped by access and sample size.
keywords: snow leopard camera trap individual data

fidelity_card.RAW: Camera-trap rosette and tail photographs in range-country programme files
fidelity_card.UNIT: One flank — tens of individuals per valley study, hundreds range-wide in files, paired-camera protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Rosette ID vs genetic ID from the large scat programmes (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Mongolia's long-term collared population as anchor

niches.headline_shape: The ghost cat's coat is the only name it answers to — twelve countries keep twelve partial ghost albums.
niches.why_niche: Snow leopard science is grant-by-grant and valley-by-valley; the global programme publishes status maps, not the pattern files beneath them.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: KILL custody in C12: rosette files are programme libraries (PAWS 1M+ images), location-sensitive by design. 7 -> 6.

niches.name: African wild dog coat-pattern ID archives
niches.family: D. Coat patterns — stripes, rosettes, spots & scales
niches.score_justification: No two painted dogs share a coat; pack catalogues per park are guide-and-researcher photo books, some running since the 1990s.
keywords: African wild dog coat pattern identification

fidelity_card.RAW: Coat-pattern ID photographs and pack catalogues from parks and den-monitoring projects
fidelity_card.UNIT: One flank — dozens per pack, hundreds per park catalogue, photo protocol at dens and sightings
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Coat ID vs ear-notch/collar identity in monitored packs (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Long-term Selous/Kruger known packs

niches.headline_shape: Every painted dog is a one-off painting — rangers name the paintings, and the name-books stay in the parks.
niches.why_niche: Pack catalogues are working tools of individual parks and guides; when a project ends, its coat archive typically ends with it.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: KILL custody in C12: no file pile on any surface probed; pack catalogues stay in the parks. 7 -> 6.

niches.name: Pangolin scale-pattern & seizure ID records
niches.family: D. Coat patterns — stripes, rosettes, spots & scales
niches.score_justification: Pangolin scales carry individual pattern and are the seized commodity itself — rescue-centre ID photos and seizure inventories are two unjoined pattern archives.

fidelity_card.RAW: Dorsal scale-pattern photographs from rescue/rehab centres and confiscated-scale inventory photographs
fidelity_card.UNIT: One scale field — hundreds of rescued individuals per large centre; seizure lots by the tonne, photo protocol at intake
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Scale-pattern ID vs DNA sampled at the same intake/seizure (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Rehab centres' known residents photographed repeatedly

niches.headline_shape: A pangolin's scales are its armour and its price tag — the rescued ones are photographed, the seized ones are weighed, and the two records never meet.
niches.why_niche: Pangolin work is split between welfare centres (photos, no genetics budget) and enforcement (genetics, no pattern archive); the pattern system itself is barely studied.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign12: KILL in C12: premise weakest of the batch - PUNS documents that programmes mark by notching, each with its own system; no individual scale-pattern archive is kept anywhere found. 7 -> 5.

niches.name: Mammal dental casts & tooth-row pattern collections
niches.score_justification: Dental casts are how mammalogy measured tooth rows before CT; cast drawers in museums carry collector-era labels that CT-era taxonomy revised.

fidelity_card.RAW: Plaster dental casts and tooth-row photographs in museum and dental-school collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One tooth row — hundreds to thousands of casts per collection across dozens of species, impression protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Cast-era species labels vs modern CT/morphometric re-identification of the same specimens (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Type specimens whose casts circulated to other museums

niches.headline_shape: Before scanners, a mammal's teeth travelled the world as plaster — the plaster is still in the drawers, wearing the old names.
niches.why_niche: Cast collections were teaching infrastructure; digitisation prioritised skulls, and the cast drawers kept their paper labels.

niches.name: Antler tine & beam record archives (trophy and cast-antler series)
niches.score_justification: Record books scored antlers for a century; cast-antler series from known bucks (same animal, yearly sheds) are growth curves hiding in trophy rooms.
keywords: cast antler collection known deer yearly

fidelity_card.RAW: Antler measurement sheets, score charts and shed-antler series photographs in record-book, agency and ranch collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One antler set — record books hold tens of thousands of scored heads; known-buck shed series run 5–10 yearly sets per animal, one scoring protocol (Boone & Crockett / SCI / CIC)
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Score-book age/identity vs the same buck's known history and yearly sheds (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Pen-raised known-age bucks with complete shed series

niches.headline_shape: The same buck drops a bigger crown every year and picks it up nowhere — hunters kept the crowns, and together they are his growth chart.
niches.why_niche: Trophy records were compiled for ranking, not biology; shed series sit with ranches and collectors, and agencies' measurement sheets were never pooled with them.

niches.name: Horn growth-ring (annuli) age records — sheep, goats, ibex
niches.score_justification: Bighorn/ibex ages are read off horn rings at check stations; the ring counts were validated on a few known-age herds and then applied continent-wide.
keywords: horn annuli age bighorn sheep data
horn growth ring ageing ibex records
mountain goat horn age validation study

fidelity_card.RAW: Horn photographs, segment-length measurement sheets and annuli counts in agency and alpine-club collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One horn — thousands of checked rams/ibex per jurisdiction across decades, tape-and-photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Ring age vs cementum age and vs known age of marked animals (second rulers)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Known-age marked herds (e.g. Ram Mountain bighorns) as the anchor

niches.headline_shape: A ram wears its birthdays as rings on its horns — check stations have read them for decades and filed the readings by district.
niches.why_niche: Horn ageing is agency routine in a dozen jurisdictions with a dozen filing systems; the validation herds are famous, the routine counts unexamined.

niches.name: Bat wing venation & membrane pattern archives
niches.score_justification: Wing veins and membrane scars ID bats in the hand; banding-era wing photographs and venation drawings sit in chiroptera collections, pre-dating the DNA revisions of bat taxonomy.

fidelity_card.RAW: Spread-wing photographs and venation tracings in bat research and museum collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One wing — thousands of banded bats per long-term study, dozens of species per regional collection, wing-against-light photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Wing-based species ID vs DNA barcode of the same banded bat (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Banding records tying wing photos to recaptures

niches.headline_shape: A bat's wing is a hand with the fingers stretched into a sail — the veins map like a palm print, and banders photographed them for decades.
niches.why_niche: Bat taxonomy was rebuilt by DNA while the wing-photo files of the banding era stayed with their collectors; nobody re-ran the old wings against the new names.

niches.name: Livestock iris-pattern ID records
niches.family: F. Faces, ears, eyes, scars, tails & whiskers
niches.score_justification: Iris ID was piloted for cattle/horses in the 2000s (IrisScan-era trials) and abandoned for RFID — the trial image sets are stranded pilots, perfect hunter shape.

fidelity_card.RAW: Iris photographs and match-score files from livestock biometric pilot trials (universities, defunct startups)
fidelity_card.UNIT: One iris — hundreds to thousands of animals per trial series, fixed-camera protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Iris match vs RFID/DNA identity of the same animals (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Trial herds with full tag records

niches.headline_shape: For a few years, cows were going to log in with their eyes — the iris trials were run, photographed, and shelved when ear tags won.
niches.why_niche: Pilot-era data lives with defunct vendors and thesis appendices; the livestock-biometrics literature cites the trials without their image sets ever surfacing.

niches.name: Ear-notch & ear-punch record systems (livestock and wildlife)
niches.family: F. Faces, ears, eyes, scars, tails & whiskers
niches.score_justification: The pig litter-notch system and cattle notch codes are pattern languages recorded on registration cards for a century — applied marks, but archived like print collections.
keywords: ear notch system pig litter identification records
ear punch code wildlife marking records

fidelity_card.RAW: Ear-notch diagrams on registration cards, breed-association records and wildlife marking logs
fidelity_card.UNIT: One notched ear — millions of pigs/cattle registered under notch codes since the early 1900s, standard notch-position charts
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Notch code as read from the card vs the animal's pedigree/DNA record (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Breed associations' master registration books

niches.headline_shape: A pig's ear is punched with its litter number like a train ticket — the ticket stubs fill a century of farm record books.
niches.why_niche: Notch systems are taught in every animal-science course and archived nowhere centrally; association card files are the only corpus and they are paper.

niches.name: Spotted hyena ear-notch & spot ID archives
niches.family: F. Faces, ears, eyes, scars, tails & whiskers
niches.score_justification: Hyena ID combines natural ear notches, spots and scars — the Mara/Talek clan archives run since 1979 with drawn ear diagrams per animal.

fidelity_card.RAW: Drawn ear-notch diagrams, spot photos and ID files from long-term hyena projects
fidelity_card.UNIT: One ear/flank — hundreds of known hyenas in the Mara archive since 1979, dozens in Ngorongoro and other clan studies, diagram protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Ear/spot ID vs genetic ID from darting samples of the same hyenas (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Known-pedigree clan members (births observed)

niches.headline_shape: A hyena's torn ear is its signature, drawn by hand into the clan file the day it is first recognised.
niches.why_niche: Clan archives are single-lab treasures (the Mara files span 45 years); no second clan's ear diagrams have ever been compared with them.

niches.name: Scar & wound-pattern photo-ID archives (cross-species)
niches.family: F. Faces, ears, eyes, scars, tails & whiskers
niches.score_justification: Scars are the accidental ID system — shark-bite scars on seals, propeller scars on manatees/dugongs, fight scars on hippos — each programme sketches them alone.
keywords: shark bite scar identification seal archive

fidelity_card.RAW: Scar sketches and wound photographs in photo-ID programme files across taxa
fidelity_card.UNIT: One scar pattern — hundreds to thousands of individuals per programme, sketch-then-photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Scar ID vs tag/genetic ID recorded at the same encounters (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Rescue/rehab animals with known identity and dated wound photos

niches.headline_shape: An animal's worst day becomes its ID card — the scar sketches are filed species by species, programme by programme.
niches.why_niche: Scar ID is always the backup system inside another programme's catalogue, never extracted or compared as a pattern archive in its own right.

niches.name: Hair medulla & cross-section pattern atlases
niches.score_justification: The second preparation of forensic hair work: medulla types and cross-section shapes keyed separately from scale casts, often by different authors for the same fauna.

fidelity_card.RAW: Whole-mount medulla photomicrographs and hair cross-section images with medullary-index tables
fidelity_card.UNIT: One hair section — dozens to 150+ species per atlas, sectioning protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Medulla-based species call vs scale-cast call on the same hairs (second ruler — the two preparations audit each other)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Vouchered museum hairs sectioned and cast in parallel in the classic atlases

niches.headline_shape: Cut a hair across and it shows a tiny patterned core — a second fingerprint inside the first, keyed in separate books.
niches.why_niche: Medulla/cross-section data rides inside the same regional atlases as the casts but was tabulated separately and never joined across regions either.

niches.name: Sheep & goat nose-print and muzzle records
niches.family: A. Skin prints — fingers, palms, pads & noses
niches.score_justification: Same system as cattle, a tenth the attention: show and sale sheep/goats were nose-printed for identity in fraud disputes; records are society-level paper.

fidelity_card.RAW: Ink nose prints and muzzle photographs in breed-society and agricultural-college collections
fidelity_card.UNIT: One muzzle — hundreds to thousands per society/college series, same ink-lift protocol as cattle
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Nose ID vs ear-tag and tattoo records for the same animals (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Agricultural-college teaching series with known animals

niches.headline_shape: Sheep were nose-printed to catch show-ring fraud — the print proved the prize ram was a substitute.
niches.why_niche: A footnote literature beside the cattle work; breed societies kept their own cards and no cross-society set was ever assembled.

niches.name: Cat nose-leather pattern records
niches.family: A. Skin prints — fingers, palms, pads & noses
niches.score_justification: Pet-ID folklore says the cat nose is unique; the actual old evidence is thin vet/clinic photo files — a claim waiting for its archive, hence the lower score.

fidelity_card.RAW: Nose-leather photographs in vet-clinic, shelter and cattery files; a small patent-era print literature
fidelity_card.UNIT: One nose — hundreds in scattered clinic/shelter photo sets, no standard protocol (that absence is itself the finding to test)
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Nose pattern vs microchip identity for the same cats (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Shelter intake photo series where chip ID is recorded

niches.headline_shape: Every cat's nose is said to be one of a kind — but unlike dogs and cattle, nobody ever built the card file to prove it.
niches.why_niche: The claim circulates in pet culture with almost no archival base; any systematic clinic photo piles sit unexamined in shelter systems.

niches.name: Hoof & cloven-track measurement systems (deer, livestock, poaching forensics)
niches.score_justification: Deer/sheep/goat/cattle slot measurements are poaching-case evidence; reference sets are police/lab-local and small, hence the score.
keywords: cloven hoof track deer sheep comparison

fidelity_card.RAW: Hoof-print photographs, casts and slot-measurement tables in forensic and game-warden reference sets
fidelity_card.UNIT: One hoof print — hundreds per reference collection, dozens of ungulate species, ruler protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species called from the slot vs the animal carcass/DNA in the same poaching case (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Farm and zoo ungulates printed on known ground

niches.headline_shape: Two toes in the mud can put a poacher in court — if the reference prints for every hoofed suspect were ever gathered in one place.
niches.why_niche: Hoof ID is casework knowledge held by wildlife forensic labs and wardens; their reference casts and photos were never published as a set.

niches.name: Claw-mark & scratch-tree archives (bears, big cats)
niches.score_justification: Claw spacing on marked trees is measured in bear/cat studies plot by plot; a real system but the archives are thin and local, hence 6.
keywords: big cat scratch mark tree data

fidelity_card.RAW: Photographs and spacing/height measurements of claw marks on trees and posts, from bear and big-cat field studies
fidelity_card.UNIT: One marked tree — hundreds per study area, tape-and-photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species/individual suggested from claw spacing vs camera-trap photos at the same trees (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Marks made by known captive bears/cats on standard posts

niches.headline_shape: A bear signs the tree it rubs — the width of its claw strokes is a signature researchers measure and then file away study by study.
niches.why_niche: Claw-mark data is a by-product of habitat studies; no cross-study archive of mark measurements exists.

niches.name: Bite-mark & tooth-pit records (predation and forensic)
niches.score_justification: Tooth-pit spacing on bones identifies the predator in fossil and modern kill studies; reference bite sets are few and lab-local — real but thin, hence 6.
keywords: bite mark tooth pit measurements predator

fidelity_card.RAW: Bite/tooth-pit photographs and spacing measurements on bone, from taphonomy labs and kill-site studies
fidelity_card.UNIT: One bitten bone — hundreds per taphonomy reference set, calliper protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Biter called from pit spacing vs DNA/feeding-trial bites by known animals (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Feeding-trial bones from known captive predators

niches.headline_shape: The spacing of two punctures in bone can name the jaws that made them — palaeontologists and wardens measure the same holes and never compare notes.
niches.why_niche: Bite-mark reference work is split between fossil taphonomy and wildlife forensics, each with small private reference sets.

niches.name: Vibrissae follicle & mystacial pad maps (small mammals & pinnipeds)
niches.family: F. Faces, ears, eyes, scars, tails & whiskers
niches.score_justification: Whisker follicle arrangements are mapped whisker-by-whisker in neuroscience (barrel cortex) and pinniped sensory labs — deep data, narrow archives, hence 6.

fidelity_card.RAW: Follicle maps and mystacial-pad photographs/drawings from sensory-neuroscience and pinniped labs
fidelity_card.UNIT: One whisker pad — tens to hundreds of mapped individuals per lab across a dozen species, dissection/photo protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Follicle-map identity vs the same animal's whisker-spot photo ID (second ruler — two readings of one pad)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Lab colonies where the same individuals are mapped and photographed

niches.headline_shape: Every whisker has an address, and the brain keeps a map of the addresses — the address books are drawn lab by lab and never compared across species.
niches.why_niche: A methods detail inside neuroscience papers; the comparative pattern data was never the point of any single lab, so nobody assembled it.

niches.name: Tail pattern & tail-ring ID systems (lemurs, raccoons, cats, marine mammals)
niches.family: F. Faces, ears, eyes, scars, tails & whiskers
niches.score_justification: Tail rings/notches close many ID calls (cheetah tail tips, lemur rings, dolphin tail stocks) but are recorded as a field inside other catalogues — thinnest standalone archive here, hence 6.

fidelity_card.RAW: Tail photographs and ring/notch diagrams inside multi-feature ID catalogues
fidelity_card.UNIT: One tail — hundreds of individuals per host catalogue, photo protocol shared with the host system
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Tail ID vs the host catalogue's primary feature (flank/face) for the same animal (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Catalogues where tail photos were taken at every encounter (cheetah, dolphin sets)

niches.headline_shape: Half of a cheetah's name is written on the last white rings of its tail — tail patterns are everyone's second clue and nobody's archive.
niches.why_niche: Tail data exists only as a column in other systems' files; a tail-first pass over those files has never been run.

niches.name: Lab-animal marking-pattern records (ear punch, toe clip, tattoo archives)
niches.score_justification: Colonies marked animals by punch/clip codes for a century; the marking logs of famous long-lived colonies are identity infrastructure that outlived the experiments — archival, hence 6.
keywords: laboratory animal ear punch marking records

fidelity_card.RAW: Marking code charts and colony marking logs from long-running laboratory and field colonies
fidelity_card.UNIT: One marked animal — thousands per colony across decades, standard punch-position code charts (several rival charts)
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Mark as logged vs genotype/pedigree of the same animal in the colony records (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Colonies with complete pedigrees (e.g. classic mouse/rat colonies)

niches.headline_shape: Generations of lab mice were named by holes punched in their ears — the punch charts are a pattern language filed with the colony books.
niches.why_niche: Marking charts were standardised locally and published as methods figures; the logs themselves are institutional archives, consulted by nobody outside the colony.
